title: Weekly pregame injury-report statuses (skill positions + OL + DL front)
description: nflverse injuries releases; pregame information by construction - the qb_out promotion family's availability signal. R70 admits the offensive line and the defensive-line front (hand-in-the-dirt positions; OLB is not front) so backtest_lines.py can measure the line-injury cascades. R91/G01: the CURRENT week is rebuilt from data/injuries.json on every run (the report replaces the release for every team it covers, and its rows carry as_of_utc); every earlier week is release-only. Runner-built.

position.description: QB/RB/WR/TE (skill, unchanged), then the OL and DL-front spellings scripts/build_injury_history.py admits (OL_POSITIONS / DL_FRONT_POSITIONS).

status.description: The report label. R91/G07: the daily ESPN report's season-class designations (Injured Reserve / Physically Unable to Perform / Non-Football Injury) are admitted as Out - a player on IR is more certainly unavailable than one listed Doubtful, which fires - and the report's own word is kept in `designation`. nflverse release rows carry their verbatim spelling, which is one of these three.

designation.description: R91/G07: the daily report's own word when it is not the emitted status, so the file never claims IR and Out are the same fact. Absent on a release row and on a report row whose word already IS the status.

as_of_utc.description: R91/G01: data/injuries.json's updated_utc, stamped on every row the daily report wrote. Present on CURRENT-week rows only. It is how a reader sees which report a designation came from, and how the next run knows which rows to rebuild from scratch - freshness, not presence, decides the current week.
